body: This place is well worth a visit. It must have once been a magnificent building but sadly it is gradually falling into disrepair. I won’t go into it’s history because you need to go and experience this, only to say that the servants quarters are now used as an orphanage for boys between the ages of 5 to 16 years of age.The site was left in trust to the Sri Lankan government with the provision the it was used as an orphanage. The entrance fee goes to the orphanage so there is not a lot left for the upkeep of the actual house, so unfortunately the house is showing signs of wear and tear with parts of the property now being unsafe and consequently people are not able to be viewed.Some of the artefacts of the house and its former owner are now in a museum in Colombo, but the house still has some treasures left, wood carvings, stain glass and an incredible staircase.I would recommend a visit here, it’s not too far from Kalutara, just a ride in a tuktuk.It’s a shame that as the Sri Lankan government are the trustees that they are not putting any money towards the upkeep and repair of this magnificent building. With the house in the state and the weather in Sri Lanka I wonder how much longer this building can survive. It would be such a shame to lose a place like this so visit it while you can.
title: Visit Richmond Castle

body: This is an undiscovered gem of a building.We went to Richmond Castle purely on the recommendation of our 'tuk tuk' driver - and what a lucky conversation to have had.Set in 42-45 acres of ground this magnificent, but crumbling Edwardian mansion has fantastic wood carving and amazing architectural features. I fear they will be lost to environmental factors in time if no remedial restoration is put in place very soon.An excellent and passionate tour guide who was extremely informative. The entrance fee goes to help the education and upkeep of some local children I am led to believe.The building and grounds are administered/owned by a board of trustees who obviously value greatly this historic building and understand its architectural significance to ths part of Sri Lanka. Just a pity that the Sri Lankan government does not provide some funds to at least stop the immediate decay and allow some sort of restoration initiative to be put in motion.A sad family story makes Richmond Castle even more poignant.An extremely worthwhile visit.
title: An amazing insight into a past age.

body: Richmond Castle, Kalutara:Richmond Castle is set on an expansive 25-acre estate, boasting an impressive yet serene structure with multiple buildings. This grand early 20th-century mansion uniquely blends Eastern and Western architectural styles. Its ornate interiors feature intricate woodwork and stained glass, while the lush, expansive gardens surrounding the castle add to its charm. Richmond Castle offers a fascinating glimpse into the opulent lifestyle of Sri Lanka’s colonial aristocracy.Lunuganga Estate:The Lunuganga Estate, the country home of renowned Sri Lankan architect Geoffrey Bawa, is a masterpiece of landscape design that harmoniously merges nature and art. Located near Bentota, this serene estate reflects Bawa’s tropical modernist style, featuring beautiful gardens, tranquil water elements, and lush greenery. A favorite spot for architecture and design enthusiasts, Lunuganga offers an inspiring view of Bawa’s visionary approach to integrating built structures with the natural environment.
title: Richmond Castle, Kalutara

body: It's manor built at the turn of the century by a local magnate holding a high position (mudliyar) under the colonial rule. The story goes that he built the house (which was a replica of an Indian Maharaja's palace) to impress the girl he wanted to marry. They had the "wedding of the century" (with the house being completed just in time to host the wedding reception) only to part ways in a rather messy divorce a decade or so later. The mudliyar is said to have lived out the last few years of life alone in a room at the famous Queens Hotel in Kandy and he had willed this property to the Public Trustee, specifically to be used for the care and education of male children. The guide will tell a slightly nicer version of this story while showing you framed photos from the wedding, which leaves you with quite a hollow feeling....Is it worth a visit? We expect so little from our Public Service, I thought the Public Trustee Department is doing a relatively ok job in maintaing the property, specially the land surrounding the house. However the house itself could do with a renovation and furniture to create a proper ambience rather than just showcasing bare walls and leaving the rest to our imagination. It would also be nice if they could build some facilities like washrooms, restaurants, seating space in the garden etc. as the house itself may not really warrant a visit. Direction: Google directions are accurate. Road conditions are good and it's very close to the Kalutara town. We have to pay LKR 100 as the entrance fee (This is for locals, not sure whether the fee is different for foreigners). There is a lady who explains (in both sinhala and english) the family tree and titles at the entrance to the house and gentleman who will take you around the house. (I think he only explains in Sinhala though).
title: A tragic tale of love

body: This is the 1 "must-see" place if you like old buildings (well this is not very old) and some intriguing history alongwith it!! I visited this place during my stay at Kalutara and am glad I did so!! The estate is sprawling and lush green and to think that a single person owned it, is staggering! There are coconut and other plantations on the property. First and foremost the entry is LKR 500 per person and a guide is provided to take you around and explain the amazing architectural and historical facets of the castle. Although it is in a state of disrepair, but the beautifully done interiors can still captivate the heart!! It's really unfortunate, though, that beneath all this sheen and glorious architecture lies a sad story of a couple who dies childless and bequeathed this property to charity. A boys hostel, for under-privileged small boys, is present on the premises as was in the will of the owner. Although we visited in last week March, it was really hot and the visit is best done in the morning hours (pls check the timings on the portal) and always better to carry drinking water, wear comfortable shoes and clothing as it involves traversing staircases in the building as well...The entire visit takes approx. an hour or so..

body: We had an excellent guided tour by one of the wardens of the property. She made us feel as if we were living in a more gracious glamorous time in this beautiful old house. Well worth a visit if you are in the area. Some interesting architectural details - he House was cooled by holes in the foundations which allowed cool air to circulate under the house and escape through small holes in the floors; little wedge-shaped openings in the roof allowed for cool air to circulate but kept rain out or birds from flying inside; the walls are 2-foot thick to provide natural insulation; a beautiful spiral staircase to a private viewing gallery overlooking the ballroom is not to be missed. The only negative was the road leading up to the car park and House - it needed to be resurfaced as it was riddled with pot holes.
title: Stunning relic of a bygone era

body: Richmond Castle is a Edwardian mansion, located near Kalutara. Built between 1900 and 1910, it was formally the country seat of Mudaliyar Don Arthur de Silva Wijesinghe Siriwardena. The building is currently owned by the Public Trustee and a must see. If you appreciate the English national trust properties I’m confident you will enjoy the history & beauty this property has to offer. Sadly due to funding, it is in a state of decay & I do hope they find funding before this treasure disappears. You can get here easily in a tuk tuk & it costs 500R per person to enter. This equates to around £2.50 pp. It’s well worth the small entry fee. The gardens & house are a fading beauty. We enjoyed a little tour inside the property & this was given by a lovely lady in her best English. The history & ambiance of this location make it a “must see” for me. Allow yourself 1hr for the visit & wear sturdy shoes if walking from the car park. The ground is uneven.
title: A fading beauty.

body: A neglected mansion of a very rich businessman in the colonial era that is open to visitors and run by the state. It is a replica of a castle in India. Material from many parts of the world have been brought to construct this palatial house of the early 1900s. The mansion is devoid of furniture but old photographs are lined up to give a glimpse of life of the couple that owned the mansion. The lady who was our guide provided a very rich and detailed account that brought to life the tragic take of the owner of the house and his wife. She should be commended highly for her commitment to the task entrusted to her . and the excellent work she is doing. Although the castle is not well maintained, the large number of visitors are not disappointed . It is well worth a visit by anyone who is interested in historical buildings and knowing more about life in Ceylon during the colonial era.
title: A peek into life of the Sri Lankan elite in the colonial era

body: Must have been an amazing house in its heyday. Still worth a look now and does not take too long. Cheap as well.
title: Intersting stopover on the way back to the Airport

body: The mansion had been built by a wealthy individual in the early 1900s copying an Indian palace, for him and his bride to move into after their sumptious wedding attended even by the colonial British Governor at the time. When they died childless the mansion was given over to the Public Trustee of the Government of Sri Lanka to run a home for destitute male children. As most things that are run by the Govt of Sri Lanka this too is not an exception. The place is poorly maintained and at places the ceiling was cracked and the paint on the walls peeling off. The photographs of the couple and their lavish wedding are very interesting and give us a peek into the lives of the super rich local people during the British occupation of the Island.
title: A splendid place of the past now poorly maintained

body: Beautiful building which is worth visiting. Building is in need of renovation but is interesting to see anyway. Is now a home for young boys (not orphans but where the family can't pay for education). Tour guide took us around and explained the history and the family story which was good.
title: Interesting tour, worth a short visit

body: On arrival I wondered why we had bothered. The house is in terrible need of renovations and care and attention. Once we took the tour and listened to the history of the house and the legacy of the owner I felt so different ; a reminder of a time long past and grander times. I was also touched by the boys orphanage legacy and amazed at how little they had, the basic classrooms and few books. Overall I'm glad we went.
title: More than meets the eye

body: A quite big mansion built in early 1900 is fast deteriorating the condition today due to poor management. Actually this is very similar to some places in India. Very historical to both British and Sri Lankan due to the last owner’s relationship. Government must do a quick restoration before it is too late.
title: A lot to be done to restore the place

body: Richmond Castle in Palathota is one of the historical large dwelling house.This considered one of the most spectacular architectural works. amassing Cooling system.. but need more attention from Government and Public.....
title: Lovely Dwelling House...

body: really pleased to have got there,not as well known as some other things there,but well worth going ,a great story to the history of the place
title: a little known must

body: Group of members with their families from Alumni Association of University of Peradeniya Colombo Chapter visited the Richmond Castle in Kalutara. It is a wonderful castle and staff working at the castle explain clearly how the castle was built. According to them owner of the castle when the Castle was handed over to the Government has put down some conditions. One of the conditions is the maintenance of the castle has to be done with the income generated from the castle and the land surround the castle. Because of that Castle was not well maintained. The Natural air cooling system of the Castle is wonderful and the colour of the glasses used for the doors and windows are changed when you look from inside and outside. We visited the Castle when we stayed at Tangerine Beach Hotel at Kalutara. Everyone who visit Kalutara must visit the Richmond Castle.
title: University of Peradeniya Alumni Association Colombo Chapter Visit to Richmond Castle

body: Well worth a visit, the architecture is very good, it's a shame that it has got quite run down, but you can see how magnificent it once was, the spiral staircase is beautiful, we had a lady guide who made the visit really interesting, I found the stories about the statues in the garden fascinating, one of the rooms is being used to teach boys, the garden is pretty and well maintained.
title: Interesting visit

body: When we went unfortunately there were no English guides.. so we only spent about half hour.. suggest you check if there are English guides before going in..
title: Okay for a visit

body: Beautiful old building with a fascinating and sad history. Guide was very nice and informative. Worth the visit as all monies go to helping the boys.
title: Beautiful old house

body: Good place to visit for a piece of history of Sri Lanka. Very good experience. Something to see if you are in Waskaduwa.
title: A Unique house

body: A really nice place to visit. Unfortunately very run down, but very interesting history.The female Guide is superb with a wide range of stories to support the facts.Really nice to do.
title: Well worth a visit

body: A wonderful way to spend an afternoon being guided round this atmospheric Castle. The lady who informed us of the tales of the past was highly informative - I had read much about the Castle but she embellished my knowledge with an impressive tale of the history of the Castle. The story of Richmond includes love and heartbreak, Maharaja's and musicians.....and now is in a sorry condition due to lack of funding. Definitely worth a visit....if even to hear the heartbreaking stories of the garden statues....
title: Extremely Interesting and a Little Sad

body: Friendly, tour of entire house cost 500 rupees, very well informed, concise and good english, easy to understand,
title: Informative

body: Richmond Castle is one of the grandest and ancient buildings in Sri Lanka. It actually gives many impressions and wonder, amazement and feeling of proudness are some.The techniques used and the buildings structure makes any visitor fall in love with this place.
title: A must-see in the area

body: A haunting castle with a tale of by gone grandeur, a broken heart and only ruins left to record a great rise to posterity. The Public Trustee of Sri Lanka should upkeep this much much better. A rambling ruin of Edwardian architecture. Well worth a visit.
title: Tour

body: This was the palace of Wijayasinge Srivardhana. He later converted to Christianity and changed his name to Arthur Silva. This palace resembles the palace of the Maharaja of Ramnad in South India.The Palace has excellent architecture with classic intricate woodwork, ventilation and cool air circulation. The wooden staircases and the spiral cast Iron staircase stands as exhibit to the architectural brilliance of those times.It has an expansive area with full of greenery. The entrance fee for non locals is Sri Lankan Rupees 500.
title: Great Architecture

body: Highly recommended for the people who are interested in Architecture, interior designing and Ceylon history. And there are guides (Actually two: one gent and one lady) who explained the history of the owner's family and the history of the building in very nicer way. Kudos to them. Beautiful house in a huge garden. I heard that this place is famous for wedding photos and pre-shoots. Good place to go if you are interested in above fields which I mentioned.
title: Good site, need some planning to it

body: As other reviewers have said, Richmond Castle is very run down and needs a lot of work. However, both myself and the friends I visited with still found it very interesting and atmospheric. There was a lot of history and an interesting background story as to why the orphanage there is only for boys. We found the tour useful and interesting, and when we began asking questions, the guide offered more information and some humour too! I just hope it receives more money for renovation before it completely decays...
title: Interesting but needs work

body: Went there last year with a friend. And we got a lady guide. She explained well about the family history and the history of this castle. According to the guide the real name of the castle is 'Rich Man's castle' which later became 'Richmond Castle'. You can see the Kalutara temple from the top floor. The architecture and interior used to build this castle is really interesting. But the place needs lot of maintenance. The visit will take less than half an hour, but it's worth it. Don't forget the camera. Recommended for people who are interested in architecture, interior and carvings,
title: Interesting place to visit before building a house

body: Have more potential if maintained well. Guide was good a well mannered informative guy. Place looked untidy.
title: Outdated

body: It used to be a very beautiful place, but not anymore. It needs a serious renovation and proper maintenance, otherwise not much would be left. Left very sad feelings.
title: Needs extensive renovation

body: An interesting heritage family home to visit on your way to Galle and the garden is very beautiful. Good place for a family with kids to visit
title: Interesting site

body: Worth a visit, a beautiful old building which is really run down, the story behind it is very interesting. The man who owned it was unable to have children and wanted a son so much! when he died he left the building to be used as an orphanage for the poor local children but only for boys. I thought the story would make a lovely film. There are some amazing photographs on the walls We really enjoyed our visit do try and visit as they desperately need the mony
title: An interesting visit

body: Richmond Castle has a certain ambience about the place. Very informative view of the past when a great gentleman lived here and did a lot for the community. Now it is a boarding school for boys a legacy of the mans will. All ticket money goes to keep up the repairs on the property. Its still a magnificent place and has a tranquil feel to the property. The gardens are extensive if you have the time to look around.
title: Visit to the past

body: As per other recent reviews this place is run down and desperately in need of repairs. We were told that the the only money they get for repairs comes from the entrance fees and the sales from the estate (cinnamon, rubber, coconuts). However the estate does not appear to be managed so difficult to see how they make much money from this. They raised the entrance fees on 1st April for foreigners from 200 to 500 Rupee. For what you get to see I think this is now overpriced. And I cant see that this will that much difference to the funds they need to restore this place. So much potential. If only they could get a cash injection. You did get a guided tour but this is almost like a recorded children's tour. Cannot recommend for new price.
title: Now overpriced

body: Despite being just over a hundred years old, Richmond castle has a story of bygone grandeur and a tale with a tragic end. Every room and corridor in the mansion seems to whisper out the story of what happened here. The story is too long to relate in this review so I would advise any visitor to first read up on it's history before visiting to get the best experience. There is a guide who will relate the story but the narration can be a bit rushed. The mansion itself is slowly decaying and showing signs of neglect. The caretakers vested with looking after the place seem to be doing their best given the funding challenges and strangely the lack of awareness by most about its existence. However, in a way the deteriorating state of the place adds to the experience and seems strangely fitting considering the sad ending to a place that briefly experienced such pomp and glory as evidenced by the framed pictures of the grand wedding that took place there.Not too far from the Kalutara town, the place is certainly worth a visit if you are in the area or passing Kalutara on the way to the southern beaches. Despite visiting on a weekend the place was not crowded (which is sad since they badly need more ticket sales to fund the upkeep of the mansion as well as the orphanage that is attached to the place).
title: A place with a tale to tell

body: A stunning building that's needing repair but don't let that put you off , it's a mere 200rs entrance fee and they desperately need the money for the repairs and ...... they also house some young orphan boys who also rely on the entrance fee money . We didn't know this or would have loved to take some sweets and toys etc , but for other visitors if you wish you can ask to meet the boys and take treats etc .The house would have been amazing in its day and the location is stunning! You get a guide to take you round and explain the building and the story
title: Interesting house

body: We found this by chance it's really quite amazing so much history the wood work carvings of the main staircase is just so beautiful. Quirky ideas that really work for keeping the Palace cool that still work. A very popular destination for school parties from all over Sri Lanka a piece of history well worth seeing. So impressive many thanks to the lovely lady who showed us around. Only 200 Rps to enter the money goes to restoration worth paying so much more to see this historical building and learn it's history.
title: So impressive

body: Having visited Richmond castle 4 times, my last visit recently was still enchanting. Is great to see more information coming forth and to see that there are many visitors. The Castle is in real need for a lot of maintenance and it is hoped that this will not be to far away. A romantic, sad and beautiful true story of the Mudiliyar and his wife.
title: trip back in time

body: This place is charming and has an intriguing history. Currently owned by the government and is slowing rotting away. Its a shame no one is looking after this tourist attraction. The entrance fees are ridiculously low. Read the history online before you visit the place. The guide you will get would be the most uninteresting/unenthusiastic person you will ever see. Beautiful architecture. I was told by one of the guides that its going to be restored soon. However the last time it got a coat of paint was in 2011. No tips allowed so avoid tipping the guides.
title: Wonderful history sliding into ruins

body: Richmond Castle has such a wonderful history it is a pity that the house seems to be degrading very quickly however the lady who showed us around was knowledgeable friendly and interesting . Visit so that the house which is now a childrens home for boys is able to be a success.On another note purple faced Langar Monkeys are nearby so you may see a few.
title: Quiet

body: Richmond Castle can be found quite close to Colombo, and boasts architecture inherited from British rule. It was built by a Sri Lankan mudliyar, and is quite extensive. Entrance fee is Rs. 30 for locals and Rs. 300 for tourists. The staff provide an extended tour of the castle with a thorough explanation on the history of the castle and its owner.
title: Colonial Castle

body: Richmond Castle is located in the district of Kalutara. Therefore, it is possible to visit this castle if you’re on the way to the south of Sri Lanka from say Colombo. It was not the easiest place to find as there was no signage directing one to the castle from the main roads of Kalutara. However, if you ask the local tuk-tuk drivers, they will direct you to the castle. From memory, I think we paid approximately Rupees 200.00 or 300.00 each to enter the castle grounds. The grounds are extensive and would be a lovely walk if only they were maintained, but sadly they are not well maintained. There is also free parking at the castle very close to the entrance.The castle itself is in desperate need of repair and we were informed that the only means of repair is from any proceeds that are derived from tourist and locals’ visits to the castle. There is apparently no funding being provided from the government or any large donations for the restoration work. Therefore the more people that visit this venue, the better, as they will then have sufficient funds to restore this once magnificent castle.We were also informed that the young boys that are being housed at the castle are also being looked after from the proceeds that come from the entrance fees to the castle.Even though the castle is in great disrepair, it is possible to visualise its yesteryear magnificence. The narration given by the guide is very good indeed, as it allows you to understand the history of the family and the castle.There were toilets available at the venue, but I suggest you look elsewhere as the facilities were extremely rustic and not very hygienic. There were no facilities to purchase refreshments at this venue.
title: Worth a visit

body: There are ten orphan boys under care of the Castle's staff. Ages,10 - 16 range to date. They are schooling. Every need of them is attended by the caring staff. But any interested visitor can see them with the staff's permission and offer individual gifts/treats etc as any human being welcome gifts.

body: During our beach stay, we went to see Richmond castle & it was interesting & worth to see.Our guide has given us interesting information about the history of this castle.loved to see this place.

body: The "castle" is an imposing building which has been allowed into a state of disrepair since the owner died but according to the lady guide is now owned by the Government and money is to be spent on it starting early 2017. There are many original sections of the building including glass made in Scotland at the turn of the century and the wooden staircase which has been repainted but a lot of money will need to be spent. The lady guide spoke very good English and it is well worth a visit at 200 rps.
title: Castle badly in need of impending improvement

body: Isolated from the hectic city of Kalutara, this place is wonderful treat to anyone who would like to see some stunning architecture, or who just wants to walk around the lovely gardens. We had a very nice tour guide that explained everything to us. I would recommend visiting Richmond Castle!

body: Our visit to Richmond Castle was organised by Mango Lanka tours. The tour guide Bob was very helpful and informative about the local area and history of Sri Lanka and was very good value. Richmond Castle offers both an historic view of how time has passed in Sri Lanka from being a British run state (Ceylon) to an independent democracy and how wealth and position in Sri Lankan society echoed the British class system. The story of Richmond castle is a very moving story in terms of loss, sadness and a wish for children to continue the family identity. It is very important to recognise the current work of the children's home located in Richmond Castle and how this is linked to its history. Well worth a visit.
title: Past and present

body: A grand building with staff who will guide you round with a great knowledge of the building and its history. It was renovated just 5 years ago but has aged again and would benefit of goverment help to keep this great looking building from ruin.Worth a visit but only for an hour.

body: Richmond Castle is a short detour off the main Colombo/Galle A2 Highway at Kalutara – unfortunately now by-passed by most people travelling on the Southern ExpresswayThe “castle” is in fact a medium sized colonial style grand mansion set in lush landscaped grounds overlooking the Kalu Ganga River. What makes this unique is that the property was conceived and built by a wealthy native Sri Lankan at a time of British colonial rule in the early 1900’s. Many of the materials including beautiful stained glass and an iron staircase from Britain imported as part of the constructionThe current building is, it has to be said, not in the best state of repair and a substantial section of the ground floor and the outbuildings have been occupied by a local nursery/pre school groupNevertheless the exterior (based on an Indian Moghuls Palace) still looks very good and inside the grand staircase and the banqueting hall give a feeling of the grandeur that the place once enjoyedThere’s also a splendid display of photographs recording the ostentatious wedding of the owner and other events and these really need to be properly conserved - If only the National Trust could get their hands on this piece of history!Entry is a few rupees and the guide who takes visitors around is extremely knowledgeableWell worth a visit as a change from visiting the usual temples in the area
title: An escape from the temples and beaches

body: Located a 10 minutes tuk tuk ride from Kalutara. Our driver Patte, was excellent. Punctual and very informative. Entry cost was 100lkr for foreigners, 20lkr for locals and 10 rupees for children.On arrival he handed us over to the Castle guide who spoke good English. She explained the history & showed us the house which is being renovated. The tour took about 1 hour. There are many photos showing how it looked in it's heyday. The house is now owned by the Dept of Public Trustee (similar to the UK National Trust) so it survives on donations & government help. Part of the grounds are an orphanage for boys whose families cannot afford an education.
title: A grand house with a sad story

body: this place is an ongoing renovation project of a rich mans dream. he wanted to copy a palace in India but the Maharajah refused him permission. So he hired two architects to go to India and survey the palace, photos everything, to get sufficient information to build his dream. When it was finished it must have been magnificent for the time because you can still see it within the buildings and the old photos. well worth the visit...there is no charge but donations are expected usually from 500skr (Sri Lankan rupees) about £2

body: The word 'castle' is really a misnomer - it is a mansion and famous for its architectural features and build during the period from 1889 to 1947. It is an estate of 42 acres and built by a wealthy landowner turned philanthropist, Padikara Don Arthur de Silva Wijesinghe Siriwardena. Queen Mary from England attended his wedding. The building once served as the home of high ranking officials of the British Administrative Service. It was the last will of the owner that the mansion be used as a Orphanage for boys which today uses part of the place. It is also used for community activities of the area. Tourists are welcome to see round the mansion, which contains several very interesting photographs.
